original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuñjanmadāśrayaḥ|
asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Hear, Pārtha, how you — with your mind attached to me (mayy āsakta-manāḥ), practising yoga, taking refuge in me (mad-āśraya) — will know me entirely (samagram), without doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Opens chapter 7 directly after 6.47 (the most yoked yogin is the one who worships the Lord with faith, his inner self gone to him).

original.text:
jñānaṃ te'haṃ savijñānamidaṃ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ|
yajjñātvā neha bhūyo'nyajjñātavyamavaśiṣyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I will declare to you, without remainder, this knowledge (jñāna) together with its realized/discerning knowledge (vijñāna); when this is known, nothing further remains here to be known.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The commentators divide on the jñāna/vijñāna pair (e.g. knowledge from scripture vs its direct experience; knowledge of the Lord's essence vs of his distinguishing modes); the verse itself only pairs them.

original.text:
manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaśicadyatati siddhaye|
yatatāmapi siddhānāṃ kaśicanmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Among thousands of human beings hardly one strives for perfection (siddhi); and even among those who strive and are perfected (siddhānām), hardly one knows me in truth (tattvataḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

tags.stage_native: yatamāna (striver) / siddha (perfected) / tattvato vettā (knower in truth)

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The segment's IAST 'kaśicad / kaśican' reflects an encoding artefact of the source Devanāgarī (vowel sign placed after the virāma); read 'kaścid / kaścin'. 'yatatām api siddhānām' is read either as 'of the perfected who strive' or 'of those who strive (and think themselves) perfected'.

original.text:
bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhireva ca|
ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Earth, water, fire, air, space (kha), mind (manas), intellect (buddhi) and I-making (ahaṅkāra): thus is this nature (prakṛti) of mine divided eightfold.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The eightfold list differs from the classical Sāṃkhya count; some commentators (e.g. Śaṅkara) take the five elements as their subtle forms and manas, buddhi, ahaṅkāra as standing for ahaṅkāra, mahat and the unmanifest; the verse itself simply lists the eight.

original.text:
apareyamitastvanyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām|
jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: This is the lower (aparā) nature. But know, mighty-armed one, my other, higher (parā) nature, which has become the living being (jīva-bhūtā), by which this world is upheld.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jīva-bhūtā' — 'which is the life-principle / which has become the jīva'; commentators differ on whether it is the field-knower (kṣetrajña) in all bodies or the totality of souls; minimal sense kept.

original.text:
etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya|
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Understand that all beings have these (two natures) as their womb (etad-yonīni); I am the origin (prabhava) and likewise the dissolution (pralaya) of the whole world.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyatkiñcidasti dhanañjaya|
mayi sarvamidaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: There is nothing whatever higher than me, Dhanañjaya; all this is strung on me like clusters of gems on a thread.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ|
praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the taste (rasa) in the waters, Kaunteya; I am the light of moon and sun; the syllable Oṃ (praṇava) in all the Vedas; sound (śabda) in space; manhood/human strength (pauruṣa) in men.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau|
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the pure fragrance (puṇyo gandhaḥ) in the earth and the brilliance (tejas) in fire; I am the life (jīvana) in all beings and the austerity (tapas) in ascetics.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam|
buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know me, Pārtha, as the eternal seed (bīja) of all beings; I am the intelligence (buddhi) of the intelligent, the splendour (tejas) of the splendid.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
balaṃ balavatāṃ cāhaṃ kāmarāgavivarjitam|
dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the strength of the strong that is free of desire and passion (kāma-rāga); in beings I am desire (kāma) that is not opposed to dharma, O bull of the Bhāratas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Some commentators distinguish kāma (craving for what is absent) from rāga (attachment to what is had); the verse only names both.

original.text:
ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye|
matta eveti tānviddhi natvahaṃ teṣu te mayi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And whatever states/beings (bhāvāḥ) are sāttvika, rājasa and tāmasa — know that they are from me alone; yet I am not in them, they are in me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'bhāva' may mean states (of mind) or existents; commentators divide.

original.text:
tribhirguṇamayairbhāvairebhiḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat|
mohitaṃ nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ paramavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Deluded (mohita) by these three kinds of states made of the guṇas, this whole world does not recognise me, who am beyond them and imperishable (avyaya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
daivī hyeṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā|
māmeva ye prapadyante māyāmetāṃ taranti te
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For this divine (daivī) māyā of mine, made of the guṇas, is hard to cross over; those who take refuge in me alone (mām eva prapadyante) cross over this māyā.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The commentators divide on the status of this māyā (an indeterminable power veiling the Lord, or the Lord's real prakṛti with its wondrous guṇas); the verse calls it divine, made of the guṇas, and 'mine'.

original.text:
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ|
māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Evil-doers (duṣkṛtin), the deluded (mūḍha), the lowest of men, whose knowledge has been carried off by māyā and who have resorted to a demonic disposition (āsura bhāva), do not take refuge in me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino'rjuna|
ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Four kinds of people of good deeds (sukṛtin) worship me, Arjuna: the afflicted (ārta), the one who seeks to know (jijñāsu), the one who seeks an object/wealth (arthārthin), and the knower (jñānin), O bull of the Bhāratas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'arthārthin' is glossed as a seeker of wealth, or of some desired object; minimal sense kept.

original.text:
teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhakitarviśiṣyate|
priyo hi jñānino'tyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of these the knower (jñānin), ever yoked (nitya-yukta), devoted to the One (eka-bhakti), is distinguished; for I am exceedingly dear to the knower, and he is dear to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The segment's IAST 'ekabhakitar' reflects an encoding artefact of the source Devanāgarī (vowel sign placed after the virāma); read 'ekabhaktir'.

original.text:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam|
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: All these are noble (udāra), but the knower I hold to be my very self (ātmā eva); for he, with self yoked, is established in me alone as the unsurpassed goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam' is read by the commentators as identity (the knower is my very self), or as the knower being the Lord's own support/dearest like his self; the paraphrase keeps the words 'my very self'. 'Noble' (udāra) = generous/exalted; all four kinds are approved.

original.text:
bahūnāṃ janmanāmante jñānavānmāṃ prapadyate|
vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: At the end of many births the one possessed of knowledge takes refuge in me, (knowing) 'Vāsudeva is all' (vāsudevaḥ sarvam); such a great soul (mahātman) is very hard to find.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Vāsudeva is the speaker's own patronymic name (Kṛṣṇa as son of Vasudeva).

original.text:
kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante'nyadevatāḥ|
taṃ taṃ niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those whose knowledge has been carried off by this or that desire (kāma) resort to other deities (anya-devatā), adopting this or that observance (niyama), constrained by their own nature (prakṛti).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati|
tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever form (tanu) any devotee (bhakta) wishes to worship with faith (śraddhā), I make that very faith of his unwavering.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate|
labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaiva vihitān hi tān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Endowed with that faith he seeks to propitiate (ārādhana) that (deity), and from it he obtains his desires — which are in fact ordained by me alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām|
devāndevayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But the fruit of those of small understanding (alpa-medhas) is finite (antavat); worshippers of the gods go to the gods, my devotees come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
avyaktaṃ vyakitamāpannaṃ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ|
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The unintelligent (abuddhayaḥ) think of me, the unmanifest (avyakta), as having come into manifestation (vyakti), not knowing my supreme state (paraṃ bhāvam), imperishable and unsurpassed.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The segment's IAST 'vyakitam' reflects an encoding artefact of the source Devanāgarī (vowel sign placed after the virāma); read 'vyaktim'. The commentators divide on the view rejected: that the Lord, formerly unmanifest, has now become manifest like an ordinary being; or that he is merely a manifest (embodied) person; the verse states only that they think the unmanifest has come into manifestation, not knowing his supreme state.

original.text:
nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ|
mūḍho'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Veiled by my yoga-māyā, I am not manifest (prakāśa) to all; this deluded world does not recognise me, the unborn (aja), the imperishable.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna|
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I know the beings that are past, that are present, Arjuna, and that are yet to be; but no one knows me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata|
sarvabhūtāni saṃmohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Through the delusion of the pairs (dvandva-moha) that arises from desire and aversion (icchā-dveṣa), Bhārata, all beings fall into bewilderment at their coming into being (sarge), scorcher of foes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'sarge' — at birth / at creation (the emission of beings).

original.text:
yeṣāṃ tvantagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām|
te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But those people of meritorious action (puṇya-karman) whose sin (pāpa) has come to an end, freed from the delusion of the pairs, worship me firm in their vows (dṛḍha-vrata).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye|
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those who, having taken refuge in me (mām āśritya), strive for release from old age and death (jarā-maraṇa-mokṣa) know that brahman entirely, the adhyātma, and action (karma) in full.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ|
prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those who know me together with the adhibhūta and the adhidaiva, and together with the adhiyajña, they, with minds yoked, know me even at the time of departure (prayāṇa-kāla).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The six terms of 7.29–30 are left undefined here; Arjuna asks about them in 8.1–2.

paraphrase: Chapter 7 (in colophons 'jñāna-vijñāna-yoga'): Kṛṣṇa undertakes to teach how Arjuna, mind fixed on him and taking refuge in him, will know him entirely (7.1–2), noting the rarity of such knowers (7.3). Movements: (1) 7.4–7 his two natures — the lower eightfold prakṛti (elements, mind, intellect, I-making) and the higher one that has become the living being; he is the origin and dissolution of the world, nothing is higher, all is strung on him; (2) 7.8–12 he is the essence in things (taste in water, light of sun and moon, Oṃ in the Vedas, the eternal seed, desire not opposed to dharma); the guṇa-states come from him, yet he is not in them; (3) 7.13–15 the world, deluded by the guṇa-made divine māyā, does not know him; only those who take refuge in him cross it; evil-doers of demonic disposition do not; (4) 7.16–19 four kinds of virtuous worshippers — afflicted, inquirer, seeker of wealth, knower — the knower being his very self, the rare great soul who after many births knows 'Vāsudeva is all'; (5) 7.20–23 those whose knowledge is stolen by desires worship other deities; he steadies their faith and grants their finite fruits; (6) 7.24–26 the unintelligent misjudge his unmanifest supreme state; veiled by yoga-māyā he is not manifest to all; he knows all beings, none knows him; (7) 7.27–30 beings are bewildered by the pairs born of desire and aversion; the meritorious, freed from them, worship him, and those who strive for release know brahman, adhyātma, karma, adhibhūta, adhidaiva and adhiyajña, and know him at the time of departure — terms that lead into chapter 8.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter title 'jñāna-vijñāna-yoga' is from the traditional colophons, not in the segments used here.

original.text:
kiṃ tadbrahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama|
adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktamadhidaivaṃ kimucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: What is that brahman? What is the adhyātma? What is action (karma), O Supreme Person (Puruṣottama)? And what is declared to be the adhibhūta, and what is called the adhidaiva?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra dehe'sminmadhusūdana|
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Who, and in what way, is the adhiyajña here in this body, Madhusūdana? And how are you to be known at the time of departure (prayāṇa-kāla) by those who are self-controlled (niyatātman)?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo'dhyātmamucyate|
bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Brahman is the supreme imperishable (akṣara); its own being (svabhāva) is called the adhyātma; the sending-forth (visarga) that brings about the arising of the states of beings is termed action (karma).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Ambiguities: 'svabhāva' is read as the supreme's own presence as the inner self in each body, or as the individual self's own nature (with its subtle adjuncts); 'visarga' as the offering/sacrifice that causes beings to arise, or as creation (emission) in general. The paraphrase keeps 'own being' and 'sending-forth'.

original.text:

paraphrase: Chapter 8 (in colophons 'akṣara-brahma-yoga') answers the terms left open at 7.29–30. Movements: (1) 8.1–2 Arjuna asks seven questions — what are brahman, adhyātma, karma, adhibhūta, adhidaiva, who is the adhiyajña in this body, and how is the Lord known at the time of departure; (2) 8.3–4 definitions: brahman is the supreme imperishable, adhyātma its own being, karma the sending-forth that makes beings arise, adhibhūta perishable being, adhidaivata the Person, adhiyajña the Lord himself in the body; (3) 8.5–8 whoever dies remembering him attains his state; one goes to whatever one remembers at the end, so remember him always and fight, with the mind held by practice; (4) 8.9–13 the meditation at departure: remembering the ancient seer beyond darkness, with steady mind, devotion and yoga-power, breath between the brows; gates restrained, mind in the heart, breath in the head, uttering Oṃ and remembering him — reaching the supreme goal; (5) 8.14–16 he is easy to reach for the constantly remembering yogin; those who reach him are not reborn, while all worlds up to Brahmā's return; (6) 8.17–19 the day and night of Brahmā, each a thousand yugas, in which beings emerge from and dissolve into the unmanifest; (7) 8.20–22 beyond that unmanifest is another eternal unmanifest, the imperishable, the highest goal and his supreme abode, the supreme Person attained by undivided devotion; (8) 8.23–27 the two paths of departing yogins — the bright (fire, light, day, bright fortnight, northern course) to brahman without return, the dark (smoke, night, dark fortnight, southern course) to the lunar light and return — and knowing them the yogin is not deluded; (9) 8.28 the yogin who knows this surpasses all the merit of Vedas, sacrifices, austerities and gifts and reaches the supreme primal abode.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter title from the traditional colophons, not in the segments used here.

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanumāśritam|
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The deluded (mūḍha) disregard me, who have taken on a human body (mānuṣī tanu), not knowing my supreme state (paraṃ bhāvam) as the great lord of beings (bhūta-maheśvara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ|
rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of vain hopes, vain actions and vain knowledge, senseless, they resort to the deluding nature (prakṛti mohinī) of rākṣasas and asuras.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ|
bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But the great souls (mahātman), Pārtha, resorting to the divine nature (daivī prakṛti), worship me with minds on nothing else (ananya-manas), knowing me as the imperishable origin of beings (bhūtādi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ|
namasyantaśca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Always singing my praise (kīrtayantaḥ), striving, firm in their vows, and bowing to me (namasyantaḥ) with devotion, ever yoked, they worship (upāsate) me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate|
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Others too, sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña), worship me — as one, as separate, in many ways — me whose faces are everywhere (viśvato-mukha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā' — commentators divide: worship as identical with the Lord, as distinct from him, and in his many forms; or three kinds of worshippers; or worship of the one Lord whose body is the manifold world. Minimal sense kept.

original.text:
ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhā'hamahamauṣadham|
maṃtro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the rite (kratu), I am the sacrifice (yajña), I am the offering to the ancestors (svadhā), I am the healing herb/food (auṣadha); I am the mantra, I am the clarified butter (ājya), I am the fire, I am the oblation (huta).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators distinguish kratu (a śrauta rite) from yajña (a smārta/daily offering); the verse only juxtaposes them.

original.text:
pitā'hamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ|
vedyaṃ pavitramoṃkāra ṛk sāma yajureva ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the father of this world, its mother, its sustainer (dhātṛ), its grandfather; the one to be known (vedya), the purifier, the syllable Oṃ (oṃkāra), and the Ṛk, Sāman and Yajus as well.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt|
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: (I am) the goal (gati), the upholder, the lord, the witness (sākṣin), the abode, the refuge (śaraṇa), the friend (suhṛd); the origin, the dissolution, the ground (sthāna), the treasure-house (nidhāna), and the imperishable seed (bīja).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca|
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I give heat; I hold back and send forth the rain; I am immortality (amṛta) and also death (mṛtyu), being (sat) and non-being (asat), Arjuna.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'sad asac ca' is read as the manifest and the unmanifest, effect and cause, or the gross and the subtle; the verse states only 'sat and asat'.

original.text:
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā
yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante|
te puṇyamāsādya surendraloka
maśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those versed in the three Vedas (traividya), drinkers of soma, purified of sin, having worshipped me with sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven (svar-gati); reaching the holy world of the lord of the gods (surendra-loka), they enjoy in heaven the divine pleasures of the gods.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'puṇyam āsādya surendralokam' — 'reaching the holy world of Indra' or 'having gained merit, (reaching) Indra's world'.

original.text:
te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ
kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti|
eva trayīdharmamanuprapannā
gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Having enjoyed that vast heaven-world, when their merit (puṇya) is exhausted they enter the world of mortals; thus, following the dharma of the three Vedas (trayī-dharma), desiring objects of desire (kāma-kāma), they obtain going and coming (gatāgata).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The segment reads 'eva trayīdharmam' where most printed editions read 'evaṃ'; the sense 'thus' is kept.

original.text:
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate|
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those people who, thinking of me with no other (ananyāḥ), worship me all around (paryupāsate) — for them, ever devoted (nityābhiyukta), I carry (vahāmi) gain and security (yoga-kṣema).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'yoga-kṣema' — acquiring what one lacks and keeping what one has.

original.text:
ye'pyanyadevatā bhaktā yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ|
te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Even those devoted to other deities (anya-devatā) who worship them endowed with faith — they too worship me alone, Kaunteya, but not according to the rule (avidhi-pūrvakam).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'avidhi-pūrvakam' — 'not by the (proper) rule'; commentators gloss it as 'through ignorance (of the Lord)', 'not in the ordained way of knowing the deities as the Lord's body', etc.

original.text:
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca|
na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For I am the enjoyer (bhoktṛ) and the lord (prabhu) of all sacrifices; but they do not recognise me in truth (tattvena), and hence they fall (cyavanti).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yānti devavratā devān pitṛ़nyānti pitṛvratāḥ|
bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those vowed to the gods (deva-vrata) go to the gods; those vowed to the ancestors (pitṛ-vrata) go to the ancestors; those who sacrifice to spirits (bhūta) go to the spirits; and those who sacrifice to me come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The segment's 'pitṛ़n' carries a stray Devanāgarī nukta; read 'pitṝn'.

original.text:
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati|
tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — that devout offering (bhakty-upahṛta) of one whose self is pure/intent (prayatātman), I eat.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat|
yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in the fire, whatever you give, whatever austerity you perform, Kaunteya — do that as an offering to me (mad-arpaṇa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śubhāśubhaphalairevaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ|
saṃnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Thus you will be released from the bonds of action (karma-bandhana) with their auspicious and inauspicious fruits; with your self yoked in the yoga of renunciation (saṃnyāsa-yoga), freed, you will come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'saṃnyāsa-yoga' here refers back ('evam') to offering every act to the Lord (9.27).

original.text:
samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ|
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the same (sama) toward all beings; none is hateful to me, none dear; but those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Stands beside 7.17 and 12.13–20 (the devotee/knower is dear to him); the verse itself states both sameness and the mutual indwelling of the Lord and his devotees.

original.text:
api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk|
sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Even if one of very bad conduct (su-durācāra) worships me with undivided devotion (ananya-bhāk), he is to be regarded as good (sādhu), for he has resolved rightly (samyag-vyavasita).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati|
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Quickly he becomes righteous (dharmātman) and attains lasting peace (śānti). Kaunteya, proclaim it for certain (pratijānīhi): my devotee does not perish.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'pratijānīhi' — 'declare/affirm (it) as a vow', or 'know for certain'.

original.text:
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ|
striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For, Pārtha, those who take refuge in me (vyapāśritya) — even those who may be of sinful birth (pāpa-yoni), women, vaiśyas and also śūdras — they too go to the highest goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators divide on whether 'pāpa-yonayaḥ' names a further class or qualifies women, vaiśyas and śūdras; the paraphrase keeps the list as the verse gives it.

original.text:
kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā|
anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: How much more then holy brāhmaṇas, and devoted royal sages (rājarṣi)! Having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru|
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Be one whose mind is on me (man-manāḥ), be my devotee (mad-bhakta), sacrifice to me (mad-yājin), bow to me; having thus yoked yourself, with me as your supreme aim (mat-parāyaṇa), you will come to me alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

paraphrase: Chapter 9 (in colophons 'rājavidyā-rājaguhya-yoga') resumes the knowledge-with-vijñāna of 7.2 as the most secret, royal knowledge. Movements: (1) 9.1–3 announcement to the non-carping Arjuna: royal knowledge, royal secret, directly evident, easy to practise; the faithless return to death-and-wandering; (2) 9.4–10 the Lord and beings: he pervades all in unmanifest form, beings are in him and he not in them — and yet they are not in him (his sovereign yoga); like wind in space; at the end of a kalpa beings enter his prakṛti and he sends them forth again, unbound by these acts, sitting as if indifferent, prakṛti bearing the world under his oversight; (3) 9.11–12 the deluded disregard him in human form, resorting to a demonic, deluding nature; (4) 9.13–15 great souls of divine nature worship him single-mindedly — singing his praise, striving, bowing — and others by the sacrifice of knowledge; (5) 9.16–19 he is the rite, the sacrifice, the fire and the oblation, father and mother of the world, Oṃ and the three Vedas, the goal, witness, refuge and friend, immortality and death, sat and asat; (6) 9.20–21 the Vedic sacrificers reach Indra's heaven and return when their merit is spent; (7) 9.22–25 he bears the gain and security of undivided worshippers; worshippers of other deities worship him not by rule and fall, each going to what he worships; (8) 9.26–28 any offering given in devotion, even a leaf, he accepts; every act is to be offered to him, freeing from the bonds of action; (9) 9.29–34 he is the same to all yet dwells in his devotees; even the very ill-conducted who worships him is to be deemed good; his devotee does not perish; those of sinful birth, women, vaiśyas and śūdras reach the highest goal, how much more brāhmaṇas and royal sages; closing injunction: mind on me, devotion, sacrifice and homage to me, and you will come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter title from the traditional colophons, not in the segments used here.
